newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister, military begin phonetap inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister, military begin phonetap inquiry.

text.p: Turkey's new interior minister began an investigation on Wednesday into allegations that a senior security official had organised phone-tapping of senior military leaders, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The military has also begun a probe into the claims against Bulent Orakoglu, former deputy head of intelligence at police headquarters, the agency said.
The military investigation will focus on whether Orakoglu had "obtained information and documents belonging to the General Staff by illegal means".
The allegations follow months of conflict between the secularist military and the outgoing Islamist-led government, which collapsed last month under the strain of the dispute.
The civilian probe order was one of the first actions taken by Interior Minister Murat Basesgioglu since he took over from a member of the Islamist-led coalition earlier this week.
Orakoglu, who was sent last week to the United States on a one-year posting, has been ordered back to Turkey since the allegations came to light.
Turkish newspapers said the phone-tapping was part of a wider attempt by the security services to spy on the military.

Former interior minister Meral Aksener said in comments to reporters that she had acted appropriately during her time in office and said there should be an enquiry if the security apparatus had overstepped its jurisdiction.
